name: Sudanese style mosques in northern Côte d’Ivoire
description: Eight mud-built mosques scattered across the savannah of northern Côte d'Ivoire, in towns such as Kong, Tengréla and Samatiguila, show how a style born in Djenné travelled south along Saharan trade routes. Look for sturdy buttresses topped with clay pots or ostrich eggs and stubby pyramid-shaped minarets. They are the best preserved of just twenty survivors from several hundred.
